scientificObservations: The bilingual description identifies one comparative judgement competence: explain the two stated routes and compare them for the same required output. Mechanism distinction supplies the chemical basis of that judgement; the text does not add hydrolysis or polyethylene recovery.

The PMMA repeat-unit formula and supplied MMA structural formula are consistent with addition polymerisation/depolymerisation. Remelting largely retains chains; the monomer route requires depolymerisation, purification and new polymerisation. Neither complete recovery nor conversion of arbitrary polymers into their monomers is promised.

Case A uses the same usable specification-compliant PMMA output: mechanical40/80=0.50kWh/kg and120/80=1.50EUR/kg; monomer route100/75=1.333kWh/kg and225/75=3.00EUR/kg. MMA intermediate is not miscounted as finished polymer.

Case B changes the quality condition, so mechanical45kg recyclate+15kg virgin PMMA requires50kg waste and yields69kWh/87EUR. Monomer route needs60/0.85=70.588kg waste and60kWh/90EUR. A genuine energy/cost trade-off replaces the case-A ranking; blend strength is supplied as tested, not linearly interpolated.

Environmental claims are appropriately conditional: energy is not a complete impact assessment, provider interest is separated from data, and omitted transport/auxiliaries/residue treatment limit inference. The two fully specified rubrics score case-specific reasoning without an automatic mastery cutoff or two-task quota.

Original official KC printed43 explicitly places this full recycling bullet at grundlegendes Niveau for GK and LK. Hydrolysis of polycondensates and polyethylene cycles are separately LK-only and are not imported.
German/English descriptions retain the same operations and boundaries. The sentence is dense but readable at SekII and stays at competence level rather than listing task calculations.

scientificObservations: The goal is one coherent supervised investigation: estimate a temperature-dependent solubility limit from own observations, graph it and explain crystal formation with the same capacity relation. Graphing, uncertainty and the concentration/saturation distinction serve that investigation rather than unrelated stand-alone routines.

Both language versions explicitly require an authorised supervised practical investigation and own data. Supplied synthetic comparison values, worked solutions and proposed logs are correctly distinguished from real later experimental performance. Current machine review cannot prove that practical performance happened.

Case A normalisation from5.00gwater gives31–33/45–47/63–65gper100gwater. For3.00gsolute/5.00gwater at20C, dissolved1.60g and equilibrium crystals1.40g, interval1.35–1.45g. Local30–40C interpolation givesS(35)55, dissolved2.75g and crystals0.25g, explicitly approximate.

The60gper100gwater40C sample is unsaturated relative to64, while the32gper100gwater20C sample is saturated; relative concentration does not determine saturation. With10gwater and3gsolute at20C, all3g stays dissolved and0.20g capacity remains.

Case B has a genuinely different, almost flat curve:0.05g/5gwater normalises to1.0g/100gwater, exceeding the0.6 model difference across20–40C. Unresolved change is not proof of temperature independence. At20C C contains1.70g dissolved, no crystals,0.10g capacity. E after losing1gwater contains1.44g dissolved and0.26g crystals, total5.70g. Total loading42.5 is distinguished from dissolved36g/100gwater.

The decreasing-S(T)modelR meaningfully reverses the usual cooling inference: capacity rises1g to2g on cooling, so all1g stays dissolved with1g capacity. Missing mass/time/temperature controls prevent attributing a real photograph to a unique cause or certifying a crystal mass. Supersaturation and delayed nucleation are correctly treated as limits of equilibrium predictions.

KNO3 oxidiser precautions, small authorised quantities, loose covers and teacher-controlled40C baths are proportionate. No unsupervised hazardous heating is instructed. Non-observations remain valid observations to analyse.
